rules.text: For a new Google Calendar or Cal.com voice booking, ask the caller to spell their name and email one at a time. Finish playing the combined read-back, then get a clear yes on a later turn for that proposal. This holds with require_booking_confirmation=false. Confirm success only after the write succeeds. Rescheduling, cancellation and other existing-booking actions follow their own confirmation rules. SMS has a separate flow.
rules.why: A new booking uses its own spelling and confirmation gate. Existing bookings, rescheduling, cancellation and SMS have their own flows.

rules.text: Cal.com does not offer an independent general call timezone for each number. It checks the agent timezone, its integration fallback, then Europe/London.
rules.instead: Use separate agents for different Cal.com agent timezones. Google Calendar honours an explicit number-calendar timezone first, then uses the agent resolution.

rules.text: For an owned number assigned to an agent, send only return_url to start Google Calendar consent. Open the returned url for the calendar owner. A competing calendar is refused. Read the number’s status after consent to confirm connection.
Supported Google Calendar settings include availability hours, timezone and invitation behaviour. These configure that number’s booking calendar.
Starting consent returns a time-limited URL. If it expires start a fresh consent flow and let the calendar owner finish it.
Start consent and read back that number’s integration status. For call-related changes read the call’s bookings.
On agent_not_assigned assign an active owned agent to that number before starting the calendar connection.
The spelling gate applies to these new-appointment voice actions. The details confirmation action excludes an existing booking.
